items.text: CNBC (7 hours ago) confirmed, Axios first reported: Negotiators reached a 60-day memorandum of understanding to extend the ceasefire and start negotiations over Iran's nuclear program. President Donald Trump still has to approve the deal. This is the most advanced confirmed deal structure of the 90-day war. The MOU has been reached at the negotiator level — Pakistan + Qatar + Witkoff (the mediator architecture confirmed by FT). What remains: Trump's sign-off. The White House dismissed this as a "complete fabrication." Trump said no nation will control shipping through the strait. This single question — who manages Hormuz after the MOU — is what stands between a negotiator-level MOU and a Trump-signed deal.

items.bold: IRAN STATE TV vs WHITE HOUSE: Iran claims Iran+Oman manage Hormuz in MOU. White House: "Complete fabrication." Trump: "No nation controls shipping."
items.text: CNBC (7 hours ago) confirmed the core dispute: Iran's state television claimed Wednesday that Tehran agreed in a draft MOU to open the Strait of Hormuz to pre-war levels of commercial ship traffic — but Iran AND Oman would manage traffic through the strait under the MOU. The White House dismissed the report as a "complete fabrication." Trump said later Wednesday that no nation will control shipping through the strait. This is the Hormuz sovereignty dispute in its clearest form: Iran's bottom line: Iran + Oman manage Hormuz (via PGSA architecture). US/Trump bottom line: no nation controls Hormuz. Hochstein (Biden energy advisor): "No matter what happens, the Iranians will control the Strait of Hormuz for the foreseeable future. It doesn't even matter what the deal says." Hochstein's assessment is the most analytically honest statement of the 90-day war: the IRGC warning shots at four vessels Thursday morning confirm it operationally. The deal, if signed, papers over this gap. The gap itself remains.

assessment.headline: DAY 90, 8:15AM THU: 60-DAY MOU REACHED BY NEGOTIATORS — TRUMP MUST APPROVE. IRAN STATE TV: Iran+Oman manage Hormuz. WHITE HOUSE: "COMPLETE FABRICATION." US-IRAN EXCHANGED FIRE THURSDAY AM. IRGC WARNING SHOTS AT 4 VESSELS. IRAN MISSILES TOWARD KUWAIT INTERCEPTED. BRENT $93.71 WEDNESDAY. HOCHSTEIN: IRAN CONTROLS HORMUZ REGARDLESS OF DEAL. INDIA: BINARY ON TRUMP SIGN-OFF.
assessment.body:
Thursday 8:15 AM IST. Day 90. The MOU exists. Trump's pen is the only thing left.

THE MOU — WHAT'S BEEN REACHED
Negotiators agreed a 60-day MOU to:
→ Extend the ceasefire 60 days
→ Start nuclear program negotiations
(Hormuz de-mining + reopening = Phase 1, as previously confirmed by WaPo)
Trump still has to approve. He said Wednesday he's "not satisfied."
The Hormuz management gap: Iran says Iran+Oman manage; US says no nation controls.

THE FIGHTING CONTINUES
US struck Iranian drones + launch site near Hormuz Thursday AM.
IRGC fired warning shots at four vessels attempting to transit without coordination.
Iran launched ballistic missiles toward Kuwait — intercepted.
IRGC targeted US air base at 4:50 AM local time.
Both sides are fighting AND negotiating simultaneously.

HOCHSTEIN'S VERDICT — THE PERMANENT REALITY
"No matter what happens, the Iranians will control the Strait of Hormuz for the foreseeable future.
It doesn't even matter what the deal says."
The IRGC warning shots at four vessels Thursday morning confirm it.
The PGSA "controlled maritime zone" graphic (May 20) institutionalises it.
The deal papers over the language. The operational reality remains.

THE NUMBERS
Brent: $93.71 Wednesday (lowest since mid-March). Rebounding Thursday.
WTI: $88.90. At $94: India OMC near-breakeven on petrol post-hike.
If Trump signs + Hormuz opens: Brent $82-85. OMC losses eliminated.

INDIA's THURSDAY BINARY
Trump signs MOU: Brent $85-88. Nifty +800-1,000 (25,000+). Sensex +2,500-3,000. Rupee 91-92.
Trump rejects: Brent $100+. Nifty -300-400. Sensex -1,000.
Trump delays: Brent $94-97. Markets cautious.

VERDICT: Day 90 — the war's 90th day — opens with the deal at its closest and the fighting at its most paradoxical. The MOU exists at negotiator level. The fighting continues at operational level. Both are simultaneously true because both sides need the deal but neither can be seen to capitulate publicly. Trump's signature is the single remaining trigger. If he signs: India's 90-day energy emergency enters its final weeks. If he doesn't: the clock resets, and Hochstein's assessment — "doesn't even matter what the deal says" — becomes the defining verdict of a war that changed Hormuz forever.

featured.title: The Strait of Hormuz and the New Logic of Chokepoint Control
featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
